elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d) requires Contractor to “defend” Company from and against any third-party claim arising from the enumerated triggers.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify and hold harmless Customer against losses resulting from covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d) requires Contractor to “indemnify and hold harmless” Company from resulting damages, losses, costs and expenses, including reasonable attorneys’ fees.

elements.element: Vendor's defense and indemnity protection must extend to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The protected parties expressly include “Company and its affiliates.”

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must apply to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d) expressly applies to “any third-party claim.”

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must cover allegations that the Services infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d)(i) covers an allegation that the “Services” infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must cover allegations that the deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d)(i) covers an allegation that the “Works,” the agreement's deliverables, infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d)(ii) covers Contractor's breach of any applicable law, rule or regulation.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must cover a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d)(iii) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Company's Confidential Information or data caused by Contractor.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d)(iv) expressly covers Contractor's gross negligence.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d)(iv) expressly covers Contractor's wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer to provide notice of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: Company must give Contractor prompt written notice of the claim.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give Vendor control of the defense and settlement, subject to customary protection for Customer.
elements.evidence: Contractor controls the defense and settlement, but may not enter a settlement imposing an obligation or admission on Company without Company's prior written consent.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer's reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Company must provide reasonable cooperation at Contractor's expense.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must be limited to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The final sentence limits Company's indemnity to “third-party claims.”

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Company indemnifies Contractor for claims arising from materials or content furnished by Company to Contractor.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Company indemnifies Contractor for claims arising from Company's breach of applicable law.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must not extend beyond Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The clause uses “only” and identifies solely Company-furnished materials or content and Company's breach of applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor must provide an intellectual-property indemnity for third-party infringement or misappropriation claims.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d)(i) provides a Contractor defense and indemnity for third-party allegations that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by Customer's modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for modifications made by Company is included.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by combinations with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion is included.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by compliance with Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for Company-provided designs, instructions or specifications is included.

elements.element: The IP indemnity must provide a remedy under which Vendor procures Customer's continued right to use the affected item.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no procure-right remedy.

elements.element: The IP indemnity must provide a remedy under which Vendor modifies the affected item to make it non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: The IP indemnity must provide a remedy under which Vendor replaces the affected item with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: The IP indemnity must provide a refund remedy if the other remedies are unavailable or unsuccessful.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d) instead states that Contractor's indemnity obligations and Company's recovery are not subject to Section 7(a)'s liability cap; it supplies no 3× annual-fees super-cap.

result.reason: The operative redline fully implements the preferred position, including all required Vendor triggers, affiliates, procedure and narrowly limited Customer indemnity. It does not satisfy the fallback because all three customary IP exclusions, all four specified remedies and the 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent; the indemnity is expressly uncapped instead. The changes are confined to the indemnity framework and related cap treatment, and unrelated liability provisions remain operative. Drafting is substantively strong, with only minor structural presentation concerns from the isolated opening subsection marker and retained numbering/typographical issues.
